Directory Navigation and File Operations
• pwd # Show current directory
• cd /path/to/dir # Change directory
• ls -l # List files with details
• mkdir new_folder # Create a directory
• rm filename.txt # Remove a file
• rmdir old_folder # Remove an empty directory
• cp file1 file2 # Copy file
• mv file1 newname # Rename or move file
Example
$ mkdir project # create directory - project
$ cd project # go to project directory
$ touch main.c # creae main.c file
$ ls –l # list all the files with details
$ cp main.c backup_main.c # copy main → backup_main
$ mv backup_main.c old_main.c # move backup_main → old_main
Task 1 - Exploring
1. Show your current directory.
2. Move to /tmp and list all files (including hidden ones).
3. Go back to your home directory.
Task 2 - Creating & Removing
• Create a directory named “project_logs”
• Inside it, create an empty file named “debug.txt”
• Copy debug.txt to debug_backup.txt.
• Rename debug.txt → debug_main.txt.
• Delete debug_backup.txt.
• Try removing the folder — observe error.
• Now delete the file inside and remove the directory.
Task 3 - Creating & Removing (1/3)
Your team lead says:
• “We’re starting Project ORION.
• I need you to create a clean directory structure, generate some placeholder files, organize them, make
backups, move some logs, archive a vendor drop, and search through files to extract important
information.”
• Tasks you must complete on next slide.
Directory Files to Create (with contents)
orion_simple
/
(root folder)

design_A.md
– 3–5 lines describing “Design A” (module, rate, interface).
design_B.md
– 3–5 lines describing “Design B” (module, protocol, constraints).
requirements.txt
– 5–8 bullets: core features & constraints for ORION.

main.c
– a tiny C program that prints Hello ORION\n once.
preprocess.py
– prints Data pipeline started.
data/
(no files directly here)
data/raw/
measure.csv
– header ts,value + ~10 timestamped rows (e.g., 2026-02-16T12:00:00Z,42).
data/processed/
(empty initially; later must contain a
copy of raw/ as import_Q1/)
logs/

– 30+ lines like INFO app: step <n> (n=1..30).
sys.log

– DB_HOST=localhost, DB_PORT=5432, ENV=dev (one per line).
prod.env
– DB_HOST=10.0.0.5, DB_PORT=5432, ENV=prod.
vendor/
(no files directly here)
vendor/drop_Q1/
(this folder will be
moved later into data/archive/)

– 2–3 lines: firmware version, date, short note.

Task 3 - Creating & Removing (3/3)
After creating the base tree and files, students must also:
•
Copy docs/design_A.md → docs/ORION_rfp_v1.md
•
Copy data/raw/ → data/processed/import_Q1/ (recursive)
•
Move vendor/drop_Q1/ → data/archive/vendor_drop_Q1/
•
Hard-link docs/design_B_link.md → docs/design_B.md (same inode)
•
Symlink docs/app_log_symlink → ../logs/app.log
•
Do safe (rm -i) vs recursive (rm -r) deletes
•
Search with grep/find (by content, size, time), and verify with ls -l, ls -i, and (if available) tree
Permissions and Access Control
• ls –l # list the files with all permissions
• chmod 660 file # change file permissions, in order: user group others, 6 = rw-, 0 = ---
• chown user:group /dev/mydevice
Task 4 - Inspect
• Run:
ls -l /dev/shm
• Identify:
• Owner
• Group
• Permission bits
Task 5 - Modify Permissions
• Create a dummy file
echo "sample" > testfile
• Change the permissions to read-write for owner & group only
• Check the file permissions again.
Task 6 - Ownership
• Create a new group “students”
• Change group ownership of the file
Process and Thread Management
• ps -ef | grep lane_detect → find running process
• pidof ./a.out → get PID directly
• strace -f -e trace=process ./lane_detect → trace forks/execs
• kill -9 <pid> → forceful termination
• nice -n 10 ./a.out
• renice -n -5 <pid>
• pstree -p <pid>
Task 7 - Identify Processes & Trace activity
1. Start a sample program or sleep process
sleep 500 &
2. Find its PID using:
• ps -ef | grep sleep
• pidof sleep
3. Trace Its Activity & observe which all system calls are logged
strace -f -e trace=process sleep 1
Inode Inspection and File Metadata
• ls –i → shows inode count; important for debugging “No space left on device” even when disk space is
available.
• stat filename.txt
• find . -inum <inode>
• df -i
Monitoring CPU and Memory Usage
• top
• vmstat 1
• free -h
